claim: EFE decomposes two equivalent ways (risk+ambiguity; extrinsic value + expected information gain); with flat preferences it reduces to Bayesian optimal experimental design / expected information gain.
agent_test: Compute EIG over the hypothesis set for candidate tests; compare to a preference-free pick.

claim: The EFE is not simply the variational free energy of the future; the natural future extension discourages exploration, so the epistemic term is a design choice (FEEF) not a theorem.
agent_test: Not directly testable; informs how we justify S7 (as chosen objective, not derived law).
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Standard EFE planning is Bellman-optimal only at horizon 1 in POMDPs; sophisticated (recursive) inference is optimal at any finite horizon but needs pruning to be tractable.
agent_test: One-step EIG test choice vs 2-3 step lookahead at equal tokens (UoT found 1-step captures most gain).
audit_note: Content is supported, but both sources are the same Friston/Da Costa group; the evidence lines a15/a16/b05/b24 are one paper (b05 lists wrong authors Paul et al. 2024), and 2608.19202 and PMC13601584 do not bear on the claim.

claim: In small tabular tasks (FrozenLake), active inference matched or beat Q-learning and Bayesian RL, mainly in the stochastic variant (98.90 vs about 65). Authors' own simulation, one task family.
agent_test: No LLM analogue; low priority.

claim: With no preferences the agent only explores and loses purposeful behaviour (null model score about 50, goal reached 44.0%): epistemic value needs a pragmatic term.
agent_test: Ablate goal term: pure-EIG test choice vs EIG+utility; expect pure EIG to wander.

claim: Both state-information and parameter-information terms are needed in simulated agents (ablations stall or fail to adapt).
agent_test: Hard to test in LLM; skip or test cue-sampling vs not.

claim: Deep (neural) active inference with information gain scales poorly in an independent reimplementation: every agent with the info term failed dSprites; 1% info gain sharply cut reward; EFE agent picked one action.
agent_test: Warns that weighting epistemic term heavily can collapse behaviour; test info-weight sweep.

claim: Other deep implementations report gains from information gain: wider state coverage, one-trial sparse MountainCar, competitive with PPO2 on Animal-AI.
agent_test: Conflicts with K07; author-run, small benchmarks. Treat as unreplicated.

claim: In stationary bandits approximate active inference beats UCB/Thompson only up to about T=10^4 trials, then regret grows faster than logarithmic; in switching bandits it does substantially better.
agent_test: Analogue: epistemic bonus helps when the problem shifts, not when stationary; test on changing-task streams.

claim: Learned preferences make agents exploit in stable worlds and keep exploring under constant volatility.
agent_test: Low priority.

claim: Picking the next question by estimated expected information gain over hypotheses improves LLM question asking over direct prompting in 20 Questions, diagnosis and troubleshooting (UoT +38.1% avg claim; BED-LLM +37.4 points; Mazzaccara EIG-trained gains).
agent_test: Same hypothesis set, same token budget: EIG-ranked test vs LLM-chosen test; measure success per token.

claim: EIG-based question selection gains are not uniform across settings: in Mazzaccara et al. the DPO gain was only +1.1 points on Celebrities (out-of-domain) and on BigBench (29 candidates) success rose 17.2 to 31.0 percent while mean EIG fell 0.31 to 0.28; in UoT, open-set gains over direct prompting are not systematically smaller than closed-set gains, and BED-LLM gains 37.4 points in an open target space.
agent_test: Report gains separately for enumerated vs open hypothesis spaces.
audit_note: UoT tables show open-set gains are often larger than closed-set gains (e.g. Llama3-70B MedDG DP 25.7 to UoT 50.6 in OS vs 60.2 to 64.3 in CS), BED-LLM gets +37.4 points in an open target space, and Mazzaccara's Celebrities +1.1 is a domain shift at the same 8-candidate size, not a larger set; BigBench success actually rose 17.2 to 31.0 while EIG fell.
claim_before_audit: EIG selection gains are larger with closed candidate sets and shrink or reverse with open or larger sets (UoT OS vs CS; Mazzaccara BigBench EIG falls 0.31 to 0.28; Celebrities +1.1 points).

claim: High EIG alone is not sufficient: Battleship question-choice by EIG gave only +0.021 to +0.026 F1; gains came only when question answers were used in move selection. Weak models also front-load questions.
agent_test: Test whether the agent actually conditions its next step on the test result (S8 update).

claim: Bayesian strategies let weak LMs beat humans in Battleship (Llama-4-Scout F1 0.367 to 0.764; win rate 0.82-0.83 vs humans); redundant zero-EIG questions fall to 0.2-1.2%.
agent_test: Replicate in a hypothesis-test game with a small model.

claim: LLMs' raw in-context belief updating is miscalibrated: they sample hypotheses incompatible with history and become overconfident; filtering for compatibility and a static likelihood help (static beat updating in most cells, e.g. Qwen Animals 95 vs 89).
agent_test: Filter hypotheses against evidence before scoring tests; compare to unfiltered.

claim: Cheaper substitutes recover only part of the gain: in BED-LLM's 20 Questions ablations, predictive entropy lands between Prompt-Only and full EIG (e.g. Animals GPT-4o-mini 44 / 79 / 88 percent; Celebrities GPT-4o 45 / 64 / 86), and LLM-judged Implicit Maximization beats Prompt-Only only modestly and works much less well than full EIG; separately, Piriyakulkij et al. show expected-entropy minimisation and expected model change are equivalent in their setup.
agent_test: Compare full EIG against LLM-judge ranking of candidates at equal tokens.
audit_note: In BED-LLM Table 1 Implicit Maximization recovers little of the gain (e.g. Celebrities GPT-4o: prompt-only 45, implicit 50, BED-LLM 86; the paper says it 'works much less well'), and predictive entropy recovers only part (about 30 to 80 percent) of the gap.
claim_before_audit: A cheap substitute works: predictive entropy or letting the LLM pick the best of sampled candidates (Implicit Maximization) recovers much of the gain; entropy and model-change objectives are equivalent in one setup.

claim: Explicit EIG with LLM-estimated logprobs can underperform implicit reasoning in code clarification (HumanEval t=10 accuracy %: EIG-logprobs 4.1 vs implicit-ToT 5.1, EIG-uniform 6.2); estimation method matters.
agent_test: Test likelihood estimator choice (sampling vs logprob).

claim: Preference elicitation: EIG/BOED-based question selection beat vanilla and ReAct prompting in a simulated shopping task (Piriyakulkij), OPEN (BOED) beat LM-only and BOED baselines in user studies (Handa), and BED-LLM beat prompt-only in simulated movie recommendation though prompt-only was a stronger baseline there; separately, non-EIG LM-driven elicitation (GATE, Li et al.) beat supervised, pool-based active learning and user-written prompts with significance in only 2 of 3 domains.
agent_test: Lower priority than hypothesis-test settings.
audit_note: Li et al. (GATE) elicit with prompted LMs (open-ended questions, edge cases) and do not use an EIG objective; their comparison is against supervised learning, pool-based active learning and user-written prompts, with significance only in content recommendation and email validation.
claim_before_audit: Preference elicitation: EIG-based questions beat prompt-only in simulation and in human studies, but with mixed effects (significant in 2 of 3 domains for Li et al.; prompt-only strong in BED-LLM movies).

claim: Measured tests of EFE in LLM agents are now two, both confounded: PUMA (2026) beats counselling baselines (Qwen3-8B Lift 1.62 vs 1.07) but bundles a world model and belief module; Dutta et al. (2026) frame OQA as EFE but only measure LLMs against a DP oracle, and their prompt-optimization EFE result is qualitative. Earlier layers (Prakki, Duraisamy, Wen) remain qualitative or position papers. No study isolates the EFE form from plain information gain.
agent_test: Do not cite as support.
audit_note: Numbers and paper descriptions check out; 'Wen' is named in the claim but has no listed source, and 'only two measured tests' is an absence-of-evidence statement from a literature search, not something the sources prove.

claim: Theory: EFE under uncertain precision yields take-the-best; more chain-of-thought hurt by 17.3 points in the high meta-uncertainty regime (CI 7.7 to 25.5).
agent_test: Single recent preprint; replicate before use.

claim: Human and animal data do not separate EFE from simpler models. Active inference fit two of four two-step datasets better than hybrid RL and about half of participants showed an information-gain weight (Gijsen 2022); it beat RL in a 25-person EEG bandit (Zhang 2025); but a heuristic-bonus RL model with perseveration fits equally well (Mathar 2025), and an older information-measure study found probability gain beat Shannon information gain (Nelson 2010). No study pits EFE against reward-plus-plain-EIG directly.
agent_test: Gap, not evidence. Optional: test probability-gain ranking vs Shannon EIG for S7.

claim: On fully enumerated attribute tables with exact posteriors, seven frontier LLMs reduce uncertainty every turn but need more questions than the dynamic-programming optimum (planning gap in figures; N=25 to 300 candidates).
agent_test: Count questions to isolate the target with LLM-chosen vs EIG-ranked tests on a table with a known optimum.

claim: Tying the information weight to what the final judge checks matters: with hand-set attribute weights and a stop threshold, compliance rose from 0.0417 (about 112 tokens) to 0.375 (about 219 tokens), while information about an unchecked attribute (tone) bought nothing. Synthetic answers, 48 tasks.
agent_test: Weight candidate tests by relevance to the final answer; ablate the weights.

claim: On underspecified math, logic and planning problems, LLMs pick the right clarifying question well for math (over 80%) but poorly for logic and planning (under 50%); chain of thought and few-shot did not help consistently, and solving the fully specified problem did not predict success. A breadth-first search reaches 99.8% at depth 10 on logic.
agent_test: For the agent, derive the discriminating test by explicit search over constraints/hypotheses, not by free choice.

claim: In humans, a probability-gain (error-minimising) measure explained information search better than Shannon information gain in experience-based tasks (Nelson 2010, three experiments, abstract-level).
agent_test: Compare probability-gain and entropy rankings of tests on the same hypothesis set; check whether they differ.

claim: In a Friston-group simulation of 64 games (32 trials each), expected information gain over models and parameters cut mean rule-discovery time from 28.5 to 19.4 trials and raised cumulative score from 89.2 to 150; removing all information gain dropped the score from 150 to 51, and the single failure with full information gain was a premature commitment to the wrong model (one simulation by one group).
agent_test: Rank tests by how they split competing explanations, include model uncertainty, and check against state-only ranking.
audit_note: The paper says the one premature commitment to the wrong model happened with full expected information gain (one failure in 64 games), not with state-only gain; the eLife paper (Schwartenbeck 2019) is about state vs parameter exploration and does not report these rule-discovery numbers; the PMC article is in Nat Commun (2026), same Friston group.
claim_before_audit: Hypothesis-level expected information gain (over candidate rules or models, not only states) speeds rule discovery in simulation: discovery time 28.5 to 19.4 trials and cumulative score 89.2 to 150 over 64 games; state-only gain caused one premature commitment.

claim: LLMs mis-time stopping in information gathering (overshoot or undershoot); trained terminators (CaRT) and a cost-vs-information stop rule (Dutta Prop 3.3) address it. No prompt-only stop rule has been measured.
agent_test: Add a stop rule: test only if expected information per token exceeds a threshold; compare to fixed test budgets.

claim: Scaffold-only EIG selection with LLM-defined likelihoods and an LLM-generated candidate list improves preference inference over vanilla and ReAct prompting with fewer user questions; expected entropy reduction and expected model change are equivalent. The comparison does not fix total tokens.
agent_test: Add an equal-token best-of-N control.
audit_note: Claim is fully supported only by Piriyakulkij et al. (2024), including the entropy/model-change equivalence; STaR-GATE is a fine-tuning method, not scaffold-only EIG selection, so there is no second independent source (the 'tokens not fixed' remark is an author caveat).
